In the United States, building a data center now polls roughly as well as abolishing the police. If current trends continue, server warehouses may soon be less popular with Americans than pizza topped with pineapple and shattered glass.
The data centers are winning
Why the AI buildout (probably) can’t be stopped.
In an August survey from Heatmap Pro and Embold Research, just 15 percent of Americans said they would support a data center being built in their area, while 75 percent expressed opposition. One year earlier, 43 percent of respondents in the same poll had approved of nearby data center development, while just 42 percent opposed it.
Key takeaways
- Data center projects are increasingly unpopular and vulnerable to local opposition.
- Nevertheless, the AI infrastructure buildout remains massive.
- The economic forces driving the data center boom are extremely strong.
- Since AI data centers can be located almost anywhere, it’s difficult to stop them from being built somewhere.
This soaring backlash is visible in other surveys — and in the actions of elected officials. In recent weeks, Wisconsin’s gubernatorial candidates sparred over who hates data centers more, Pennsylvania’s center-left Gov. Josh Shapiro enacted new restrictions on AI infrastructure projects (after previously championing such investment), and even Texas’s staunchly pro-business Republican government announced a temporary moratorium on new approvals.
Meanwhile, data center projects are being canceled at a record rate, as local opposition mounts.
This has led some in the pro-tech minority to worry that the data center buildout is about to collapse — and take the US economy down with it. Anti-AI commentators, for their part, are cheering the industry’s impending crisis.
But such panic and celebration are both premature.
In truth, despite exploding opposition, the data center boom is still going strong. Interviews with industry experts and recent construction data suggest that the economic forces driving the buildout remain more powerful than the political winds blowing against it. And unless Congress enacts a national moratorium, AI companies will almost certainly be able to continue finding jurisdictions willing to tolerate hyperscale campuses, in exchange for sufficient revenue and incentives.
America’s data center boom can be slowed and geographically shifted. But it probably can’t be killed, absent a collapse in demand for computing power or a much bigger revolution in American politics.
The boom is bigger than the backlash
There are two fundamental facts about today’s data center boom: 1) The backlash against it is huge, and 2) the buildout is even bigger.
The climate news outlet Heatmap has kept a tracker of new data center restrictions and cancellations. As of late July, it found that more than 500 jurisdictions had enacted severe constraints or bans on data center construction. The vast majority of these measures had been enacted since the beginning of this year.
The publication also found that contested data center projects face a skyrocketing cancellation rate. In late 2024, 20 percent of disputed developments were canceled; in the first half of 2026, that figure was closer to 50 percent. By Heatmap’s tally, more than 100 data center projects have been nixed this year in the face of local opposition, while more than 200 are currently being fought.
This surge of mass resistance is remarkable. And yet, it is also nowhere near sufficient to end the AI buildout.
Although the number of places with severe restrictions (or outright bans) on server farms is rapidly rising, more than 90 percent of US counties had no significant constraints on data center development at July’s end.
What’s more, many of the most eye-catching recent policy changes are less significant than they appear. For example, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s pause does not actually halt data center construction in the Lone Star State. Rather, it essentially establishes a more thorough screening process, when server farms apply for electricity from the state’s grid. Projects that supply all of their own power through on-site natural gas — as a rising share of new data centers do — are exempt.
Pennsylvania and New York’s recently enacted restrictions on data center development are more substantial. Yet neither of those states are particularly important to the AI buildout. Taken together, New York and Pennsylvania host only about 6.5 percent of America’s data centers, according to Data Center Map.
And their share of all pending developments is even more negligible, as the trade publication Construction Connect has illustrated:
Meanwhile, although half of contested data center projects are now failing, many still go undisputed. In the aggregate, cancellations have not kept pace with construction or new development. In the first quarter of this year, at least 3.5 gigawatts of data center capacity were canceled amid local opposition, in Heatmap’s tally. During the same three months, at least 36 GW of capacity were added to the US pipeline of proposed and active projects, according to the analytics firm Wood Mackenzie. As of April 1, that pipeline contained a total of 106 GW worth of developments that had already survived the permitting gauntlet.
To be sure, cancellations have risen sharply since March. By Heatmap’s count, at least 13 gigawatts of capacity have been nixed so far this year. But the capacity of permitted projects has also grown since April 1. And the ratio between blocked and active developments has not radically changed, according to industry analysts.
“At this point, we do not think the recent wave of opposition and policy intervention has materially changed our national capacity growth trajectory,” Maya Barkin, an analyst at the AI industry research firm SemiAnalysis, told me.
Indeed, monthly construction spending on data centers in the US hit a record high this June.
In short, data centers are marching forward despite taking heavy fire, like a pack of gut-shot zombies.
The secrets of the AI buildout’s success
Why has the AI buildout proven so resilient? There are at least two reasons.
First, and most importantly, demand for computing power remains astronomical. As frontier AI companies have built out larger models — and consumers and companies have increased their use of artificial intelligence and digital services — our economy’s appetite for computation has far outstripped supply. According to a recent report from the commercial real estate firm JLL, 99 percent of North America’s data centers are occupied. What’s more, of the 66 GW of data center capacity currently being constructed in JLL’s count, 95 percent has already been reserved.
Second, data center projects are unusually location-flexible. If a housing developer gets chased out of San Francisco’s suburbs by zoning rules and local opposition, it can’t relocate its condo tower to a mostly uninhabited stretch of Nevada desert. By contrast, data centers can — and do — operate in the middle of nowhere.
For certain purposes, these facilities need some proximity to the users they serve; you can’t adequately support online gaming in New York City with data centers on the West Coast. But even in such cases, servers merely need to be in the same broad region. The hyperscale facilities used to train AI models, meanwhile, can be located virtually anywhere with land, fiber optic cables, a modicum of labor, and electricity (and now that many data centers are powering themselves through on-site natural gas plants, even the latter is potentially expendable).
Taken together, these two realities make data center construction extremely difficult to choke off. Sky-high demand for compute means that hyperscalers can afford to throw a lot of money at localities, in order to secure a project’s approval. And location flexibility makes it very difficult for data center developers to run out of host jurisdictions, particularly when so many rural counties throughout the United States are starving for revenue and investment. Thus, unless Congress imposes a national moratorium, development deals will almost certainly keep getting struck.
“I think companies will need to open up their wallets and make sure that communities receive clear benefits,” John Arnold, a billionaire investor and philanthropist who sits on Meta’s board (and whose foundation has given funding to Vox), told me. “There will be places that raise their hands and say, ‘For X amount of benefit, we will welcome you into the community.’”
Just this week, West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey signaled that he was moving forward with plans to encourage data center development and use the consequent revenue to slash the state’s income tax.
Municipal permitting won’t preempt the robot apocalypse
On one level, all this may seem to validate anti-data center activism: If there are countless potential locations for these facilities, then why should any community host one it doesn’t want?
This said, many oppose new data centers out of concern for their aggregate impacts, rather than their local ones. Climate activists fear that the AI buildout will generate perilous increases in carbon emissions. Populists on the right and left, meanwhile, want to slow the progress of artificial intelligence, so as to prevent the technology from causing mass unemployment — and/or human extinction.
For these factions, the buildout’s resilience has more complicated implications. If state and local bans are unlikely to end the boom, then green groups might be unwise to push for such measures in relatively climate-conscious areas. After all, doing so could shift development toward jurisdictions with less renewable energy, and/or fewer restrictions on carbon pollution. Given that risk, blue-state environmentalists may do more to mitigate AI’s climate impacts by regulating data center development than by banning it. Specifically, climate groups could demand that hyperscalers help bankroll the vast expansions of clean energy and transmission infrastructure that the green transition has always required.
For AI doomers, on the other hand, local bans may have some instrumental value. Moratoria and other restrictions are surely slowing the data center buildout at the margin. Still, as long as hyperscale facilities remain location-flexible — and tech companies stay well-capitalized — AI infrastructure will get built somewhere. A national moratorium could buy significant time. But ultimately, humanity’s security from the risks of AI hinges less on whether data centers get built than on what companies are allowed to do with them — and how the wealth they generate is distributed.
The data center rebellion is among the most remarkable popular movements in recent memory. But it is arrayed against one of the largest investment frenzies in human history. Unless or until the AI industry’s alleged “bubble” bursts, its buildout will be exceptionally difficult to stop. Yet where that buildout happens, how it’s powered — and what communities extract from it — are all up for grabs (and, increasingly, being grabbed).

Iran-US war latest: Tehran hits back after Trump strikes Iranian tankers and wedding party
Local officials say five people, including a child, were killed in US strike on wedding party
Iran has vowed to respond with “crushing and devastating blows” after US strikes killed five people attending a wedding party in Iran.
Iranian state media reported explosions across southern coastal areas, including Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island. Tehran also said US strikes hit civilian sites in Hormozgan province and a civilian airport in Kerman province.
One of the strikes hit a home in Kuhestak where a wedding ceremony was taking place, killing five people, including a child, and wounding at least 68 others, according to Hormozgan provincial officials.
The US military also struck two Iranian government tankers, Axios reported, marking the first time Tehran’s tankers were hit.
Iran responded by launching ballistic missiles towards Jordan, with its military saying it had targeted a US base near the Gulf of Aqaba.
The US military said it was aware of reports of civilian casualties but stressed that it “never targets civilians”.
Centcom said it concluded its latest barrage against Iranian military targets on Tuesday night. The fresh strikes came after Donald Trump said he wants “total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing”.
Pictures show wedding party where five people were killed
Five people were killed and 50 wounded at a wedding near Sirik, a coastal area on the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Red Crescent reported.
The Mehr news agency said a 4-year-old child was among those killed, while the IRNA news agency, citing a provincial official, put the number of wounded at 68.
According to reports, a shrapnel from the US strike struck a home where a wedding celebration was taking place.
Car hits pro-government gathering in Iran, killing four
A car struck a gathering of supporters of Iran's government and armed forces in the northeastern city of Mashhad overnight, killing four people and injuring more than 10, several Iranian media reported on Wednesday.
A car travelling at high speed first collided with another vehicle, lost control and then veered into the crowd after hitting safety barriers and traffic signs, Noor News reported, citing Mohsen Mousa-Abadi, head of Razavi Khorasan Province's traffic police.
Initial checks showed the driver, who was arrested, was not in a normal state, Mousa-Abadi said, without giving details on his condition.
There was no immediate indication of a political motive, and authorities described the incident as a traffic accident.
The evening gathering was one of a series of recurring events attended by supporters of the Islamic Republic and its armed forces since the war with the United States began in late February, according to Mehr news agency.
Iran says it is striking US assets across Gulf region
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had launched attacks against US assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Erbil in Iraq, as Tehran retaliated for fresh US strikes on Iran.
It was after Bahrain’s defence force said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks targeting the kingdom.

Bahrain’s defence force said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks targeting the kingdom.
It came as Tehran was retaliating against US strikes across the region.
Oil prices rise for second day after US-Iran strikes
Brent crude futures rose 1.3 per cent to $95.91 a barrel on Wednesday, marking further gains for a second day after fresh US strikes on Iran pushed oil prices higher.
The latest exchange of strikes has raised concerns over further disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices rose to a five-week high on Tuesday after the strikes began.
"The threat of further disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz has brought about renewed anxiety over inflation, driving a selloff in stocks across most major markets and a rout in global bond markets," Westpac analysts wrote.

Bollywood actor Hrithik Roshan has entered into a five-year lease agreement for a commercial office space in Mumbai’s Goregaon East. According to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix, the actor has leased the 2,727 sq. ft. premises to QuantumX Global Private Limited for an estimated total rental value of Rs.4.84 crores over the lease period.
Hrithik Roshan leases Mumbai office space for Rs. 4.84 crores; actor rents 2,727 sq. ft. property to QuantumX global
The office is situated on the 14th floor of the E-Wing at Lotus Corporate Park, located within the Graham Firth Steel Compound in Goregaon East. The registered agreement was executed on August 31, 2026, as per the property documents.
The lease carries a duration of 60 months, translating to five years. The registered agreement states that both the licence commencement and rent commencement dates have been fixed for September 5, 2026.
Under the terms of the agreement, the rental amount will be subject to a 5% annual escalation. The initial monthly rent has been set at Rs.7.30 lakhs. With the stipulated yearly increase, the monthly payment is expected to rise to around Rs.7.67 lakhs during the second year of the lease.
The rent would subsequently increase to approximately Rs.8.05 lakhs per month in the third year, followed by nearly Rs.8.45 lakhs in the fourth year. In the fifth year, the monthly rental obligation is projected to reach approximately Rs.8.87 lakhs, assuming the agreed 5% escalation is applied successively each year.
Based on these terms, the cumulative rental amount for the complete five-year tenure works out to approximately Rs.4.84 crores. The calculation assumes that the annual escalation outlined in the registered agreement is implemented throughout the lease period.
The commercial property transaction adds to Hrithik Roshan’s association with Mumbai’s premium real estate market. The actor has previously been linked to investments and properties in the city, while Goregaon East has emerged as a significant commercial and entertainment hub with several office developments.
As of now, Hrithik Roshan and QuantumX Global Private Limited have not commented on the reported lease transaction. The details regarding the agreement are based on the property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.

Quick Answer
Instagram uses icons for likes, comments, reposts, saves, messages, Reels, Stories, calls, profile tools, notifications, active status, and more. This guide explains what every major Instagram symbol means and what happens when you tap it.
Instagram is the most popular app with billions of users around the world. The platform has lately been getting plenty of new features and fixes.
Instagram is also one of the few platforms that are known for experimentation. Meta often changes their layout very often, which can sometimes confuse users. If you are new to Instagram, or even an existing user, the new features and some icons you never use can be confusing.
Some of the features on Instagram don’t have an undo option, so it is better to know what they do before pressing them. In this guide, you will learn everything about Instagram icons, their meanings, and what they are used for. To make it easy for you, we have included each and every icon on every page of Instagram and explained what it does.
Table of Contents
What Do Instagram Symbols and Icons Mean?
Instagram Post Symbols Meaning
Instagram posts are what we see and interact with most on a daily basis while using the app.
They come with several engaging elements. Most of them are easy to understand, but if you are confused, here is what they mean:
- Like: Wherever you see this heart symbol on Instagram, it represents a like for posts, comments, and all
- Comment: This represents a comment on the post. Tapping on it reveals all the comments, and you can also add a comment.
- Repost: Instagram has recently introduced the ability to repost. The reposted post also appears on your feed.
- Save: The save feature lets you save posts; in other words, it works like a bookmark.
Instagram Home Screen and Bottom Navigation Bar Icons Meaning
Now let’s look at what the icons mean on the home screen and on the bottom navigation bar.
You won’t find many icons on the home screen, except for the ability to create a new post and to view all your notifications.
If there is one area that Instagram constantly experiments with, it is the bottom navigation. Meta keeps changing the positions of the icons and also changes their designs frequently.
Here is what they mean:
- Notifications: The heart symbol here represents notifications. Here, you can see all the notifications you receive inside the Instagram app.
- Create: The plus symbol here represents “create,” which you can use to create a post or a story and more.
- Home: Tapping on the home icon takes you to the home screen. It is part of the main bottom navigation. Tapping on it also takes you to the latest posts.
- Reels: Instagram has added a dedicated Reels tab, where you can tap on it to go to the Reels section.
- Messages: Tapping on this icon takes you to the Instagram Messages screen, previously known as DMs.
- Search: Tapping on the search icon takes you to the Explore page.
- Profile: This is a profile icon, which takes you to your profile page.
Instagram Reels Tab Icons Meaning
Instagram offers a dedicated Reels tab where you can see all the latest Instagram Reels. It also comes with several interactive elements, some of which are already used for posts.
Here is what each and every icon means in the Instagram Reels tab:
- Create: You can also add new posts directly from the Reels page. You can tap on the Plus icon.
- Like: It lets you like the Reel you are watching. You can like it, and tapping on it removes your like.
- Comments: Lets you add a comment and see comments for the Reel you are currently watching.
- Repost: It lets you repost the Reel you are currently watching.
- Share: It lets you share the Reel with your friends. You can also copy the Reel link using this option.
- Save: You can save or bookmark the Reel using this icon.
- More options: Gives more options for Reels, including Playback controls, Meta AI, and much more.
- Audio: It represents the audio used for the Reel. Tapping on it reveals more details.
Instagram DM Page Icons Meaning
Instagram DMs are among the most feature-packed, yet Instagram somehow manages to keep them minimal. However, they do come with several icons. Here is what each icon means in the Instagram message space:
- New message: It lets you create a new message. After tapping, you can select the user and send a message.
- Notifications off: It appears if you turned off notifications for Instagram.
We missed highlighting the Instagram Instant feature that the company introduced very recently. It lets you share a random photo with other users without complex editing.
It is turned on by default, and tapping on it shares whatever your phone camera sees, so be careful before pressing it. There is also an option to turn it off completely
Instagram Profile Page Icons Meaning
Instagram profile page also comes with plenty of icons. Here is what they mean:
- Create: Lets you create a new post, Reel, or Story from your profile page too
- Menu: Lets you access main and global Instagram app settings
- Threads: Lets you open the Threads app by Instagram.
- Discover people: The icon lets you discover new friends. It appears when you have a lower following count.
- Posts: Represents the Posts tab
- Reels: It represents the Reels tab
- Tagged posts: It represents the tagged posts where you can see all the posts you were tagged in by your friends.
- Pinned post: It means the user has pinned the post. Instagram lets the user pin up to three posts.
Instagram DM Message Icons Meaning
The chat interface also comes with plenty of icons, which can be confusing for a beginner. Here is what each icon means inside Instagram chats:
- Instagram Blend Feature: This is an Instagram Blend feature where you can invite the user to the Blend, where you can see each other’s suggested Reels, new Reel suggestions based on the chat, and much more.
- Voice call: Lets you make a voice call to the user
- Video call: Lets you make a video call to the user
- Voice message: Lets you send a voice message in the chat
- Photo library: Lets you select the local photos on your phone and send them to the chat
- Stickers: Lets you access the stickers
- More options: Gives you more options, including the ability to send location, draw, and access Meta AI and much more
- Camera: Lets you access the camera, where you can quickly take a photo and share it with the user.
Instagram Share Screen Icons Meaning
The share screen on Instagram is very simple. It is very similar to the other share screens, but it comes with one unique icon that lets you create groups. Here is what that icon means:
- Create group: This is the share screen that appears when you tap on the share button under the post or the Reel. The user icon means you can create a new group.
Instagram Call Screen Icons Meaning
Instagram calling screen also comes with several icons during the call, and here is what each of them means:
- Camera off: During the video call, it lets you control the camera. If you see a cross line, it means your camera is turned off
- Mute microphone: Lets you mute or unmute your camera
- Speaker off: Lets you turn on or off sound from the other user
- End call: End the video or voice call using this button.
Instagram Story Editor Icons Meaning
If you are adding a story for the first time, it can be confusing because Instagram Stories are feature-packed and let you customize everything you upload. Here is what each icon means on the Instagram Stories screen:
- Add text: While adding an Instagram Story, tapping on this icon lets you add text
- Stickers: It lets you add stickers to an Instagram Story
- Music: Lets you add and select music.
- Effects: Lets you add effects
- More tools: More creator tools. Tapping on it lets you access more tools
- Next: Once added, you can move to the next screen while adding a Story
Instagram Profile Bio Options Icons Meaning
Instagram profile bio also comes with plenty of icons. Here is what each icon means and what it does:
- Notifications: Lets you turn on or off notifications for this account.
- More options: Gives you more options about the Instagram profile you are viewing
- Profile link: Instagram lets users add links in their bio. The link icon represents the link the creator added to their Instagram bio. It is also available for regular users.
More Instagram Profile Icons Meaning
Here are more icons that you see when you visit any Instagram profile, including icons in the top right corner of the post and the verified blue checkmark right next to the profile. Here is what they mean:
- Verified badge: Instagram has verified the account, which means it represents the official account. Also, Instagram allows users to pay for the verified badge.
- Video or Reel: If you see this on top of the post, it means the post contains a video or Reel.
- Carousel post: If you see this with a number, it means it is a carousel post.
Instagram Reels Controls Icons Meaning
In the Reels tab, when you pause the Reel, Instagram displays more icons. Here is what they mean, including the recent Friends tab icons:
- Create: The plus icon lets you create a new post or Reel
- Trending audio: If you see an arrow next to the audio file name, it means that audio is trending
- Sound: Lets you turn off sound or turn on sound for the video. It appears when you tap on the video
- Play: It appears when you pause the video. Lets you play the video again
- More options: Again, tapping on this option gives you more Reel options
- Reposted by a friend: If you see a purple arrow icon, it means the Reel is reposted by your friend. If you see the like, it means the Reel is liked by your friends.
More Instagram Messages Icons Meaning
Here is what the different icons mean in the Instagram DM space. If you have multiple accounts and unread messages, Instagram will notify you with different color badges. Here is what they mean:
- Pinned chat: It appears when you pin the chat for any user in your Instagram DMs.
- Muted chat: It means you muted the chat. You won’t receive any notifications for their messages.
- Unread message: It shows the unread messages inside the chat. If it appears, it means you have unread messages.
- Account switcher: Lets you switch between accounts, and if you see the red icon, it means you have unread notifications from the other account
More Instagram Post Icons Meaning
Instagram recently launched collaborations, which allow users to collaborate with each other and publish posts. It joins with older tags, the ability to add music, and much more. Here is what each icon means:
- Collaborative post: Instagram lets you add collaborative posts. If you see multiple profile pictures, it means it is a collaborative post from those accounts.
- More options: It lets you access more options for the posts
- Explicit audio: If you see an E icon right next to the sound or audio, it means the song contains explicit content
- Tagged people: It lets you view all tagged users for the post. Tapping on the user takes you to their profile
- Sound: It lets you mute or unmute the sound for the post.
Paid Instagram Post Icon Meaning
You don’t need a special introduction for the ads on Instagram. If you see a post and you are confused about whether it’s a regular post or not, you can find a little “Ad” label under the profile.
- Ad: If you see Ad, it means it is a sponsored post or ad inside the Instagram feed.
Instagram Story Viewer Icons Meaning

For 26 days, India watched as Sonam Wangchuk wasted away. His hunger strike, held in solidarity with India’s “Cockroach” youth protest movement, would prove to be one of the most politically consequential fasts held in the country’s modern history.
Many in the country view the gruelling fast, which began on 28 June, as the crucial spark that helped propel the Cockroach movement into one of the most formidable challenges to the government of prime minister, Narendra Modi, in more than a decade.
Abhijit Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach movement, said Wangchuk had “awakened the conscience of an entire nation” through his sacrifice.
The Cockroach movement was launched in May, following the cancellation of a key nationwide exam to enter medical college after a paper was leaked. The cancellation was devastating for the 2 million students who had already sat the exam, a dozen of whom reportedly took their lives.
The movement took its name from comments made by India’s chief justice, Surya Kant, who had compared some unemployed young people to cockroaches and parasites in a court hearing.
Dipke’s demand for education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, to show accountability for the leak by resigning struck a nerve, and anger that had been seething below the surface surged out on to the streets.
The protest ballooned into a nationwide movement. For weeks, deadlock prevailed between the government and Dipke, backed by thousands who flocked to his sit-in protest in Delhi. Eventually, after an unprecedented police crackdown which further influenced public opinion in its favour, the protesters triumphed and Pradhan resigned on 25 July.
The victory was not a foregone conclusion and Dipke has acknowledged the importance of Wangchuck’s fast in determining the outcome. Unlike the students, Wangchuck was a well known and respected figure, recognised for his decades-long efforts to secure educational reforms and environmental protection. Last year, he was arrested in Ladakh on charges of inciting anti-government protests.
The timing was also key: crowds at the Delhi protest site had been thinning before he started his fast on a stage there on 28 June, injecting new energy and momentum into the movement.
Wangchuk had declared he would not end his strike until the government had listened to the demands of India’s protesting youth. He lay outdoors at the Cockroach protest site in the heart of Delhi, day and night, enduring rain, torturous heat and mosquitoes. Already a lean and slight figure, he lost 11kg over the 26 days.
“I felt confined, trapped … like a prison,” he told the Guardian. “The heat and humidity were awful.”
In the aftermath, Wangchuk, a softly-spoken engineer, environmentalist and educationist, remains humble about his role. “I was a known entity and that helped,” he said. His reverence is reserved for the hundreds of thousands of young people in the Cockroach movement, which he says has changed Indian politics for good.
Wangchuk is adamant that the Cockroach movement’s success is far bigger than a single resignation. In an era where dissent is routinely criminalised, young people, he said, had seized back the power of political protest.
“They have stripped away the curtain of fear that existed,” he said. “They are now engaged. They have tasted success in getting results and I expect them to continue.”
The 60-year-old admits the hunger strike took a gruelling toll. By the time he broke his fast on 24 July, he had pushed his body to the limit and was perilously close to organ failure. But as thousands of young people and politicians flocked to his side, his spirit remained unbroken throughout.
The greatest test, he says, came when he was forcibly removed by police from the protest site and taken to hospital against his will. Videos of his frail body being dragged away by burly police went viral and Wangchuk was hailed by young people online as a national hero. When mass protests erupted the following day, Wangchuk’s name was chanted and held aloft on placards.
Wangchuk was not always an obvious figure of anti-government resistance. Born in Ladakh, he rose to international prominence as an engineer and environmentalist, best known for inventing the ice stupor, a unique technique for water storage in human-made glaciers. He became a prominent champion of the rights of Ladakhis and set up his own school and cultural and environmental institution.
He had been a vocal supporter of several prominent policies of Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) but it soon turned to resistance as he accused the BJP of failing the people of Ladakh. Last year, as protests in Ladakh escalated, he was imprisoned by the government for almost six months under draconian anti-terrorist laws.
While his focus has been on rebuilding his body in recent weeks, regaining about 60% of his previous weight, Wangchuk has also continued his call for political reform, albeit without any overt criticism of the Modi government.
In a video message posted before India’s independence day in August, Wangchuk called for a “second independence movement” and urged Indians to choose men and women of “character and substance” to lead the country.
He has urged people to share the names of individuals of integrity who can be trusted and once he has a list, he plans to meet them in Mumbai and Delhi to discuss how elections can be cleansed of those with a criminal background.
“Indians have to trust those at the top,” he said. “At the moment, there is no trust in anything, not in elections, not in exams, not in civil servants. Clean and honest leaders are the first step to a better future.”
He expressed his support for the decision by the Cockroach movement to resist calls to become a political party and instead focus on being a pressure group, championing issues of education. “When we used to talk during the long days of the fast, I used to advise them that being a pressure group is the best way to keep clean and neutral,” he said.
For now, he is back living quietly in Ladakh, finally able to enjoy the one food that lingered on his mind during his hunger strike. “I did dream of apricots,” he said, “but that was just because I was wondering if mine back home had ripened.”

Mark Carney has rebuked Donald Trump’s administration and urged officials in Washington to “start being serious” amid escalating trade tensions between the US and Canada.
Days before Canada is due to retaliate against Trump’s sweeping tariffs with its own duties on US goods, the Canadian prime minister criticized US officials for insulting his country. “It is beneath their office,” he said.
“When the Americans stop doing memes, stop throwing shade, stop trying to be tough and start being serious about having those discussions, we can have those discussions” about trade, Carney said.
Trump signed an executive order last week directing the US federal government to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America – a move that has been rejected by Canadians.
The US president’s most senior trade negotiator has meanwhile downplayed the potentially disastrous effects of a US trade war with Canada, declaring the spat to be “more their emergency than ours”.
The US trade representative, Jamieson Greer, argued that Canada was more vulnerable after the breakdown in talks set the stage for sweeping tariffs between the two neighbors, telling Politico: “There are no negotiations happening on trade right now.”
The comment comes just more than a week after US-Canada trade talks imploded. The US levied 50% tariffs on $20bn in Canadian goods.
Canada, the US’s second-largest trading partner, announced it would impose retaliatory tariffs on $20bn of American goods starting on 8 September. Now, US residents are poised to feel extreme pressure from Trump’s tariffs and Canada’s retaliatory measures, including on day-to-day items.
Greer appeared to blame the escalating trade war on Canadian officials, telling Politico: “It’s not clear Canada wants a deal.
“If Canada believes that prohibiting and banning American goods and services is appropriate, then obviously that’s something that the United States should consider as well.”
Unacceptable asks from Canada included lighter taxes on heavy-duty trucks, according to Greer, who said such requests torpedoed the trade talks.
Canadian officials, on the other hand, attributed the collapsed negotiations to a White House disagreement over who was directing trade talks. Mark Carney, the country’s prime minister, also said that American negotiators saw the French language in Canada as an “irritant”, but added: “In Quebec, these are rights.”
Trump, for his part, has argued in recent weeks that Canada “wants the benefits” of being a US state, without being one – a preoccupation of the US president – as he lashed out at the country’s leaders. “They have also charged our great farmers, for many years, massive amounts of tariffs,” claimed Trump. “No more!!!”
Greer suggested that negotiations broke down after a misunderstanding around what was, and wasn’t, on the table. “Was that political? I don’t know,” he told Politico. “Was it economic? … I’m not sure how much economic sense it makes because the choice is not between the current tariffs and … you know, duty-free trade. Like, that is that. Those weren’t the options.”

Deadlines, acrimony and a record as Man City back Maresca for Fernandez deal
- Published
Manchester City's desperation to bring in midfielder Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea not only ends the summer's longest running transfer saga but highlights the club's determination to get the deal done for manager Enzo Maresca's top target.
City have paid a joint-British record £125m deal for the Argentina international to break their club record transfer fee for the second time this summer following the £116m arrival of Elliot Anderson.
City had to overcome numerous obstacles to finalise a difficult deal during the 79-day transfer window, from being set deadlines to complete the deal and the backdrop of former Chelsea boss Maresca's acrimonious appointment as their manager.
But shelling out a joint-British record fee showcased City's perseverance to acquire their man and those upstairs at Etihad Stadium have shown unequivocal faith to both player and manager.
City have started the season with back-to-back Premier League wins and Fernandez's arrival means he becomes the first player in football history to move for more than £100m twice after going to Chelsea from Benfica for £107m in 2023.
The 25-year-old also joins a unique trio of players that have broken the British transfer record twice in their careers during the Premier League era along with former England internationals Alan Shearer and Rio Ferdinand.
All that means City's acquisition of Fernandez matches the amount paid by Liverpool to Newcastle for striker Alexander Isak on the same day last summer.
How have City pulled off the biggest deal of the summer despite a seemingly bitter relationship with Chelsea following the appointment of Maresca as manager earlier this summer?
- Man City agree £125m deal for Chelsea's Fernandez 
  - Published7 hours ago
Why City wanted to bring in Fernandez
When Maresca was appointed as Pep Guardiola's replacement in June, the Italian apologised to his former club Chelsea for the "disruption" caused by his mid-season departure.
Senior City sources had told BBC Sport at the time that they held no ill feeling towards Chelsea and that the now-resolved contractual dispute was between the Stamford Bridge club and Maresca.
And that has played out in this deal happening.
The manager was the key factor in this blockbuster deal with Maresca keen to reunite with his former Chelsea skipper.
It is understood Maresca wanted Fernandez as someone who he can fully trust and rely on, a player that is familiar with the manager's instructions, the patterns of play and does not need to be learn how to operate in the middle of the park in the system.
The 46-year-old had a similar approach when being appointed as Chelsea manager in 2023, signing Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall having worked with the player at Leicester during their Championship-winning campaign.
Looking back on Friday's pre-match news conference, Maresca had hinted at a late incoming by saying he was hoping to add "a captain" to his squad before the end of the transfer window.
City have lost the experience of Bernardo Silva, John Stones and Rodri this summer, with Ruben Dias taking the captain's armband and Erling Haaland being part of the leadership group.
Fernandez adds big-game know-how to City's midfield after winning the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, being named young player of the tournament, and helping his country to a second-straight final in July.
His antics during the summer may not make him a universally popular figure but Fernandez comes across as a player that team-mates love to have alongside them and one that gets under the skin of the opposition players and supporters.
City had been interested in signing Chelsea's Pedro Neto and Malo Gusto earlier this summer but were seemingly put off by the respective asking prices and, at that stage, Fernandez was not a player that Maresca had necessarily asked the hierarchy to sign.
However, the departures of Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez meant there was a gaping hole left in the middle of the park that needed filling.
Eyebrows were raised when Maresca deployed centre-back Marc Guehi in a holding midfield role in the opening game against Bournemouth, with the player himself saying he was surprised by the change in position.
That alteration came about as the deal for Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi had not been completed, so Guehi played alongside fellow England international Anderson.
The ownership have now splashed out £125m on Fernandez and deemed it as being worth the hefty fee for their new manager - they can also point to delivering a player who could be the final tool needed for Maresca and his men to challenge on all four fronts this season.
Though City claimed a domestic cup double in Guardiola's final season in charge, they fell short in the Premier League and Champions League so Maresca will now be under pressure to fare better in both of those competitions.
Why Chelsea had to let him go
Under Maresca at Chelsea, Fernandez helped the club win the 2025 Europa Conference League and the Club World Cup later that summer but noises emerged at the start of this year about him wanting to leave.
It began once Maresca left Stamford Bridge in January and two months later, following Chelsea's Champions League exit, Fernandez said he did not know whether he would be at the club next season.
His first choice was to join Real Madrid but the La Liga giants never came in with an offer, feeling the Premier League midfielder was overpriced.
New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso spoke to Fernandez this summer in an attempt to try and change his mind and for him to stay, but the player's heart was set on leaving.
Having been jeered by his own supporters during the home pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad, there was only one direction of travel thereafter and that exit was seemingly rubberstamped after being left out of the wins over Luton and Brighton.
A deal with City was finally struck with just hours remaining in the transfer window, but which club will feel they came out on top?
Chelsea had set an arbitrary deadline of 14 August for clubs to match their £120m valuation of the player - which passed without any offers coming in - and they were understood to be holding out for £135m on Monday.
City had indicated they would walk away from the deal at the price, instead offering £125m the following day, which was subsequently accepted.
City got their man, while Chelsea received £5m more than what they initially asked for.
Chelsea have now raised more than £425m through player sales, including add-ons this summer and fees from loan deals are expected to take that figure closer to £500m.
Club sources initially indicated they would bank the cash and not bring in a direct replacement but, with time running out on deadline day, they performed an extraordinary pivot by agreeing a £47m deal to sign Monaco's Lamine Camara.
But there was one final twist at 23:00 BST as the window closed, with the Ligue 1 side reneging on the written agreement after renegotiating a deal to sell USA striker Folarin Balogun to Everton.
It left Chelsea with the Fernandez cash in their pocket but without a replacement and, though they could have pulled the plug on the deal, the Blues decided to honour their word and allowed him to join City.

Enough new coalmining projects were proposed last year to increase global supplies by 2.5bn tonnes a year, an increase of 11% from the year before, even as demand for coal plateaus, according to a new report.
Global Energy Monitor, an NGO, found that India ignited a rise in new coalmine proposals in 2025 despite a global slowdown in the number of mine openings because of falling demand for the fossil fuel.
The increase was driven almost entirely by the states of Jharkhand and Odisha, which doubled their proposals for new coalmines in line with an ambitious plan from India’s ministry of coal to increase the country’s output.
India plans to increase its coal production by nearly 100m tonnes to 1.15bn tonnes in the 2025-26 fiscal year to help meet the country’s rising demand for electricity to support economic growth and contend with heatwaves, which have become more severe and more frequent because of the climate crisis.
The planned increases come despite signs that the world is beginning to turn its back on coal in favour of renewable electricity, Global Energy Monitor said.
Coalmine proposals slowed in the years after the Covid-19 pandemic but have begun to climb again, raising concerns that mining could increase in the future despite a slowdown in the number of new facilities.
The startup of new coalmining projects has fallen steadily in recent years, according to the Global Energy Monitor’s latest report.
It found that enough new coalmines to produce about 113m tonnes each year began operations last year, down by 40% from 2024, which was already the lowest annual total in a decade.
This was largely owing to a slowdown in new mines in China and Australia, which fell by 44% and 96% respectively.
Global Energy Monitor warned that India’s rise in new mine proposals was at odds with the slowdown in global coal demand predicted by the International Energy Agency for the end of the decade.
Wind and solar power surpassed coal generation in the global electricity mix for the first time last year, according to a separate report from energy thinktank Ember, in a “milestone moment” for climate action.
China and India were largely responsible for the rise in renewables, according to the Ember report, while the US and Europe continued to rely more heavily on fossil fuels.
Tiffany Means, a senior researcher at Global Energy Monitor and co-author of the report said: “The economic rationale for expanding coalmining becomes progressively weaker as low-cost clean energy continues to displace coal.
“Rather than locking in decades of additional coal production, governments have an opportunity to cancel projects that remain in the development pipeline before they advance to construction.”

Late-night transfer fallout sparks Chelsea-Monaco row
- Published
One source with connections to both Chelsea and Monaco said the clubs had "played with fire and got burned".
Indeed, the late-night transfer drama that involved Folarin Balogun, Everton, Monaco, Lamine Camara and Chelsea saw all parties lose out.
Camara - a 22-year-old Senegalese international midfielder - had been a target for Chelsea as they prepared for the £125m sale of Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City.
But Monaco were adamant he was going nowhere for the fee Chelsea were willing to pay.
"I've been speaking to them for the last 10 days," said Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro said.
"At around 16:00 BST yesterday we got contact from Chelsea. The answer was the same: no."
Instead, the Ligue 1 club had allowed United States international striker Balogun, 25, to fly to Merseyside to complete a £40m move to Everton. According to Monaco, Camara had agreed to stay with the club.
With three hours remaining of the transfer window, Chelsea were content with their midfield options, despite the sale of Fernandez, after failing with enquiries for Camara and Roma's Manu Kone.
But issues with Balogun's Everton medical saw the door open again for Chelsea at the £47m price point Chelsea had previously offered. Negotiations were back underway with Monaco at 20:00 BST.
Meanwhile, Everton failed to find alternatives to Balogun and revived their move with minutes before the deadline.
Chelsea had completed all the necessary paperwork for Camara and did not need to submit a deal sheet - a request to the Premier League for additional time to complete a transfer, post the deadline.
But the plug was pulled. Monaco acknowledge Camara was disappointed after he had spoken to manager Xabi Alonso, passed a medical and signed a contract until 2033.
"What happened was that around 22:00 BST our time, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised there was no issue and decided they were ready to sign the contract [for Balogun]," Scuro told reporters on Wednesday afternoon.
"As soon as we received that information, we came back to Chelsea and said there was no deal. Because that's also fair. It's part of the game."
Chelsea were left furious, claiming Monaco informed them in writing that the deal would not proceed rather than communicating the decision by phone.
Monaco thought - by signing a deal sheet, five minutes before the 23:00 BST deadline, to allow Everton extra time to complete the transfer of Balogun - they had secured the sale they needed to help comply with Uefa's financial regulations.
The Ligue 1 side were under pressure to generate 150m euros in player sales this summer, and had raised 106m euros from departures.
Balogun U-turn
Another twist was still to come.
In the early hours of Tuesday morning, the former Arsenal striker had a change of heart which saw him leave Everton's Finch Farm training ground without signing for the club.
Scuro claims Balogun felt he was mistreated while at Everton's training ground, something the Premier League club disputes.
"We had to respect his decision," Scuro added.
"We found solutions, challenged the medical assessment and worked through the issues.
"I don't want to create a war with Chelsea or Everton.
"My role is to protect Monaco and act in the club's best interests. That's what I've done since I arrived.
"It's not about being loved by people outside the club. It's about doing what Monaco needs."
Scuro says it is possible Monaco will look at selling other players to countries whose transfer window remains open in order to acquire the funds they need.
He is open to welcoming back both players and says he expects Camara to be back with "full power" for their upcoming match away at Paris St-Germain on Friday night.
"I really understand because a player can get excited by conversations with a coach and by everything a club like Chelsea can offer," Scuro continued.
"This is not the end of the world. It's one opportunity. For a player with his level of talent, I'm very confident he will soon have even better options and offers than the one he had yesterday."
According to sources close to Camara, Liverpool also retain a long-standing interest in a future deal.
Questions remain for Chelsea
Chelsea had been considering Camara as an option to replace Fernandez for the final 10 days of the window.
Of course, the Londoners could have forced a deal through sooner but it might have meant overpaying because, as sources had previously explained, Monaco saw Camara as not for sale throughout the majority of the window - barring those few hours on Tuesday evening - but for "exceptional" offers.
Chelsea were blindsided by the collapse of the deal and there was little they could have done to revive it or sign an alternative before the deadline.
They did, however, have the option of cancelling Fernandez's move to Manchester City but opted not to do so out of a sense of "professionalism".
Chelsea wanted a midfielder to replace Fernandez but there was never any desperation as the club only wanted to do so on its own terms.
Alonso sees captain Reece James primarily as a midfield option, alongside Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and new signings Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco within his 27-man squad.
Yet injuries to Caicedo and Henderson, coupled with James' workload, meant full-back Malo Gusto was used in midfield during the 4-3 victory over Brighton, a match in which Chelsea recorded 25.6% possession, their lowest figure since records began in 2003-04.
Alonso could have selected Barco, 21, who came on as a second-half substitute, but the club want to carefully manage the signing from Strasbourg as he returns to the Premier League after a short-lived spell at Brighton.
There remains debate over whether Chelsea have sufficient depth and quality in midfield, with the club retaining the option of revisiting a move for Camara or another midfielder in January.
They could also look to strengthen other positions having been left delighted at making a net profit in the transfer market while adding quality.
Chelsea signed World Cup winner Emiliano Martinez, France international Maxence Lacroix and club-record £117m signing Morgan Rogers, as well as experienced striker Danny Welbeck and full-backs Pep Chavarria and Marco Palestra.
It's now on the manager and squad they have built to attempt to match Chelsea's ambitions on the pitch, starting with Sunday's trip to champions Arsenal.

River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
- Published
Nepalese hydropower workers have told the BBC about the catastrophic moment water from the Trishuli River crashed into their tunnel as the region was inundated by deadly flash floods last week.
It started with a sudden, strong gust of air, says Pemba Dundu Tamang, whose team of about 30 was constructing the tunnel's concrete lining.
The blast of wind sent plywood flying through the air and dislodged heavy machinery. Just outside, houses had already been swept away.
"I ran towards the tunnel entrance," he said. "The water was chasing behind me and I was running ahead of it."
Tamang lost several family members who were at home at the time. Nepal's death toll has exceeded 1,000 after last week's devastating floods, and officials say about 4,000 are missing.
A number of the missing - potentially in the hundreds - are labourers like Tamang, working in a vast network of tunnels at hydropower sites along the river. Engineers have been pumping air into these tunnels as part of a huge rescue operation.
"We are focused on search-and-rescue efforts at the tunnels, our work is continuing," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP news agency.
"Our soldiers are also deployed to collect bodies and prevent the spread of disease."
Tamang says he ran for about 20 minutes to flee the violent deluge, which followed him uphill.
"I was almost unconscious with shock. I could not think clearly."
His colleague, Itha Ghale, says the powerful gust of air almost blew them away as they sprinted.
Over 99% of the electricity generated in Nepal comes from hydropower, and Tamang and Ghale had been working at a major production site helping to build the Upper Trishuli 3B Hydropower Project.
The plant, which was due to open next year, was designed to re-use water from a hydroelectric plant further upstream to generate additional electricity for Nepal's national grid.
There were several different teams operating there - and Tamang says the one operating the large tunnel-lining machine was the last to come out.
But soon afterwards came a crushing realisation.
"I could see where my house should have been. There was nothing left. That was when I realised everything was gone."
Six of Tamang's relatives - his mother, elder brother and sister-in-law and three of their children - are gone, he said. They were at home on the riverside when the floods hit.
Only his wife, son and one nephew survived.
"I feel life is meaningless now. Surviving feels miserable. I do not know where to eat or where to go," Tamang says.
"The dead are at peace. It is those of us who survived who suffer."
Ghale, who lost eight members of his family, says he does not know why he survived. "Perhaps it was not my fate to die."
The eight family members include his mother and eldest daughter. His three sons and wife survived.
Tamang dreads what the future may bring, especially if these hydropower projects are shut down. "If things continue like this, we will go hungry. Sometimes I feel it would have been better not to survive."
Tamang ultimately managed to take refuge with a few others in the village of Shanti Bazar for two days until the army came to rescue them.
He estimates about 50 to 60 workers were able to escape the tunnel alongside him.
He says more people could have been saved if proper resources had been in place.
This is echoed by a new report which says there was evidence of growing instability around the glacier in the days before the disaster - and that better early warning systems could have saved lives.
Satellite images suggest the glacier surface was moving faster, meltwater was turning brown and a crack was developing in the surrounding rock, according to experts from the Asian Mountain Academic Alliance, the Stimson Centre and China's Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment.
These are all possible signs the mountainside was becoming unstable.
The avalanche itself moved too fast for conventional warnings to help those closest to it, the scientists say.
But further downstream, where the flood took 10 minutes or more to arrive, they say a comprehensive warning system could potentially have saved a significant number of lives.
Right now, however, specialists from China, India and Nepal are continuing to use excavators and heavy machinery to blast through debris from the hydropower projects to try to reach workers still trapped at several hydropower sites.
"There are probably still some survivors inside. I would be happy if they were rescued quickly," Tamang says.
"I know many people who are still trapped there."

- Social media posts allege U.S. President Donald Trump's mother, Mary Anne MacLeod Trump, once called him "an idiot with zero common sense" and predicted he would be a "disaster" if he ever entered politics. The rumor is unfounded.
- The alleged quote has circulated since at least 2019. On multiple occasions, Snopes has attempted to find evidence of Trump's mother making the statement without success.
- Some posts spreading the alleged quote included images that resembled newspaper clippings. We have found no evidence of any real newspapers attributing the quote to Mary MacLeod Trump.
- Snopes will update this report if additional information surfaces.
An alleged quote by Mary Anne MacLeod Trump, the mother of U.S. President Donald Trump, expressing doubt about her son's intelligence and ability to succeed in politics has circulated for years.
A meme with the quote that spread on Facebook in August 2026 read:
Trump's mom knew best!
"Yes, he's an idiot with zero common sense, and no social skills, but he is my son. I just hope he never gets into politics. He'd be a disaster."
Mary Anne Trump: Telling the truth before it was trending.
(Facebook user JOE BIDEN 2024)
Snopes readers wrote in to ask us whether the quote was real.
Versions of the alleged quote have circulated for years, usually with the part reading "I sincerely just hope he never gets into:" ending with the word "politics." We've hunted for evidence the quote was real since 2019 and have found no proof that Trump's mother ever said these words. Other publications, such as PolitiFact and Reuters, also fact-checked the quote and found no indication it was real.
Because digital archives of newspapers, books and magazines grow and change over time — meaning it is always possible for new evidence for historical claims to become available — we took another look at the quote after it began circulating again in 2026, during Trump's second term as president.
In short, just as in 2019, there was no compelling evidence supporting the claim that the quote is authentic, as of this writing.
Searches for the full alleged comments — as well as the distinctive clauses "he's an idiot with no common sense" and "I just hope he never goes into politics" — on Newspapers.com and Gale OneFile, both of which are large databases of periodicals, uncovered no evidence supporting the quote's authenticity. Searches on Google Books and the Internet Archive likewise returned no evidence that the quote ever appeared with secure attribution in any legitimate publication.
A Google search found no instances of the alleged remark at all before 2019, nearly two decades after Mary MacLeod Trump's August 2000 death. The absence of any evidence of a quote dating within the alleged originator's lifetime is a common red flag for fake or misattributed quotes.
One development since 2019 was the emergence of the supposed newspaper clipping featuring the in-question comment underneath a photo of Trump and his mother, which appeared (archived) to have first circulated (archived) online in June 2020. Examples of the clipping, which did not include the name of the paper in which it was allegedly published or a date, appeared (archived) in numerous (archived) posts on X (archived).
(X user @RobertCStern)
It has not been possible to find proof that the clipping is genuine. Although it included a genuine photo of Trump and his mother that was prominently featured in a 2016 New Yorker article titled "Donald Trump's Immigrant Mother," searches uncovered no instances of the picture paired with the quote in any real newspaper or magazine.
It remains possible that a primary source proving the quote's authenticity exists somewhere — for example, in a newspaper archive that has not been digitized as of this writing — and for that reason we've refrained from issuing a definitive rating.
Previously, we looked into the claim that Trump's mother was an immigrant in the country illegally.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on August 17 announced a new national social media team, replacing Amit Malviya with Deepak Mhaskey as its IT cell in-charge. The party also named four new social media co-convenors — Priti Gandhi, Shivanand Dwivedi, Alok Bhatt and Arun Yadav.
Alt News had earlier reported that within minutes of BJP’s announcement, a search on X revealed that the accounts of the four social media co-convenors had either vanished or their posts had become inaccessible. However, screenshots and archived versions of their past tweets, often containing personal and contentious opinions, are available, raising concern over the sudden disappearance of their accounts. Yadav, for instance, deleted more than 60,000 posts before making her X handle accessible again. Mhaskey deleted at least 1,342.
Gandhi’s X account, which has over 500,000 followers, remains ‘protected’ or hidden from public view at the time of this article being published. A notice from the platform states “Only approved followers can see @MrsGandhi’s posts”.
An earlier screenshot of her profile captured by us shows her following 2,015 handles, which has now gone down to 1,875. In other words, she has recently unfollowed 140 X users.
Alt News spoke to Gandhi, and asked her why she had hidden her X posts, but she refused to comment. Her Facebook profile bio describes her as ‘IT & Social Media National In-charge for all 7 BJP Morchas’ and ‘Official Spokesperson, Maharashtra BJP’.
Recently, in November 2025, Gandhi courted controversy after targeting Indian cricketer Jemimah Rodrigues over her expression of faith during a post-match interview. After India’s semi-final victory against Australia, in which Rodrigues was named Player of the Match, she acknowledged her teammates’ support, said she had put her faith in God, and thanked Jesus in the post-match interview. Criticising this, Gandhi argued that while wearing the Indian jersey, Rodrigues represents Indians and “not her church”.
In her older tweets dating back to 2012-13, she expressed disdain for her surname, saying she would rather have ‘Modi’ or ‘Godse’ as a surname. She has repeatedly praised Nathuram Godse, the assassin of Mahatma Gandhi, in her tweets.
Declaring herself as a “huge fan and follower” of Godse, she has multiple tweets announcing that she “misses him” and that there is a need for “1000 more Godse’s” and that “India misses him.” Much of that record, however, is no longer readily accessible, but screenshots of her past tweets are shown below:
Long-time BJP Supporter
Her association with BJP, however, predates her formal organisational role. Gandhi has been a pro-BJP voice since around 2012. Initially, her X (then Twitter) handle was @pritirules. Aafter her anti-Congress posts were being shared by prominent BJP leaders, she changed her handle to @MrsGandhi. “I realised this name has a lot of potential, as there would be one Gandhi questioning the other. So I changed my handle,” she explained to the Telegraph.
In 2012, Modi started following Priti Gandhi on Twitter. According to her, she put forward her opinions aggressively — which caught Modi’s attention. Gandhi was even invited to Gandhinagar to meet Modi. “He [Modi] liked that I, as an independent person, defend him on social media”, Gandhi told The Telegraph.
In January 2014, Gandhi had falsely claimed that Julian Assange, the founder of WikiLeaks, had stated that “Modi is incorruptible”. Gandhi allegedly amplified a fake endorsement of Modi by Assange, featuring a poster of Assange alongside a quote that read, “America fears Modi because they know he is incorruptible.”
WikiLeaks responded:
#India: Here is the BJP’s Pritti Ghandi pushing fake #Assange endorsement of #Modi to 40k people https://t.co/kh8HsMlgqi
— WikiLeaks (@wikileaks) March 17, 2014
History Of Misinformation
Gandhi’s rise within the BJP’s digital ecosystem closely coincided with a long record of disseminating and amplifying misinformation. Alt News has fact-checked her claims repeatedly over the years.
For instance, in 2019, Gandhi circulated an edited video suggesting that Rahul Gandhi wanted to leave India and settle abroad. In 2020, Gandhi revived the ‘potato-gold’ remark, a claim that stemmed from a clipped video with distorted context, to mock Rahul Gandhi and mislead people.
In 2021, during the second wave of the COVID-19 pandemic, Gandhi also shared a misleading video purportedly showing an absence of crowds in Haridwar during the Kumbh Mela. The post appeared amid intense scrutiny of the religious gathering, where millions of pilgrims had assembled, and thousands of COVID-19 cases were subsequently reported among attendees and seers.
The video, however, did not depict the principal pilgrimage area around Har Ki Pauri. It was reportedly shot at Govind Ghat, several kilometres away, and at a time when the location did not see large crowds. The video was therefore misleadingly presented as evidence that Haridwar was not crowded during the Kumbh Mela.
During the 2021 West Bengal post-poll violence, Alt News had fact-checked a doctored video shared by Gandhi showing men wielding swords while dancing to the TMC election song, ‘Khela Hobe’.
In another instance, Gandhi shared a misleading video claiming that “Modi Modi” slogans were being raised inside Pakistan’s Parliament. Alt News found that the chants were actually “Voting Voting”.
More from the Archives: Propaganda & Disinformation
A recurring feature of Gandhi’s social media activity over the years has also been the amplification of communal or polarising misinformation.
In 2020, she shared an image of Priyanka Gandhi embracing the mother of the Hathras rape victim and described the woman as “fake Naxal-bhabi”. She falsely accused both Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi of consoling the “Naxal operative who had infiltrated the family’s home and was posing as the victim’s sister-in-law”.
The same year, she also circulated a clipped video of journalist Arfa Khanum Sherwani speaking about the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), using the edited clip to distort the context and present the speech in a communal light.
A Newslaundry article cites a 2021 Centre of the Study of Organised Hate (CSOH) paper, which identified Gandhi among BJP figures who amplified the ‘Love Jihad’ narrative in the aftermath of the killing of Nikita Tomar – a student who was shot outside her college in Ballabhgarh by a Muslim youth.
According to a 2020 report by Lokmat, Gandhi said in a tweet on October 27, 2020, “Those in denial of the existence of Love Jihad are only closing their eyes to reality, maybe even purposely. Unless we don’t accept the problem, finding a solution is impossible. Today it is Nikita, tomorrow it could be you!”
It is important to note that the chargesheet of the Nikita Tomar case had no sections of the IPC related to forced conversions and other associated crimes, as per a Times of India report.
In 2019, both Gandhi and Bengal BJP shared a clipped video to falsely claim a communal bias in a speech by then Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee. They shared a 12-second excerpt of her speech clipping out the part where Banerjee had recited Hindu scriptures. Alt News had fact-checked this.
In 2021, Gandhi shared a video of a man apparently blowing on food, suggesting that he was spitting on it, giving the footage an explicitly communal framing. In 2022, she claimed that participants at a Popular Front of India (PFI) protest in Pune had raised “Pakistan Zindabad” slogans. Fact-checkers found that the slogan was in actuality “Popular Front Zindabad”.
Again, in 2022, while sharing a photo of Rahul Gandhi with a girl, Gandhi falsely claimed that she was Amulya Leona, who raised ‘Pakistan Zindabad’ slogans during the anti-CAA protest in Bangalore in 2020. In reality, the girl with Rahul was Miva Jolly, an activist associated with the Kerala Students Union, the student wing of the Congress party.
During the 2024 farmers’ protest, Gandhi shared an image claiming a farmer was seen sitting on a Mercedes car worth Rs 3 crore, thereby portraying that the protesters were ‘rich’ and thus the movement was not legitimate. It was found in an investigation by Alt News that the car was actually an SUV Gurkha by Force Motors whicbh had been modified to look like a Mercedes vehicle. We spoke to the owner of the car as well.
In January 2022, Gandhi falsely claimed that Uttar Pradesh BJP MLA Vinay Shakya had been kidnapped after he had been pressured by Samajwadi Party to join them. Local police replied to her tweet clarifying that the abduction claim was entirely false. Gandhi, then, deleted her tweet.
Target of Misinformation Herself
Priti Gandhi herself became a target of misinformation when a viral thread in 2021 shared three genuine screenshots of her old posts alongside a fabricated tweet claiming that her husband had escaped the Capitol Hill riots. The thread, which gained over 10,000 likes and was amplified by several journalists and Congress members, falsely portrayed the manufactured tweet as part of a pattern in which Gandhi’s husband had narrowly escaped multiple major incidents. While three screenshots were genuine and referred to same incident (the 26/11 Mumbai attack), the Capitol Hill tweet was fake.
